audit.whatIsWrong: The whole lane plan is built on 'trade just after he burns Scrap Shield'. Scrap Shield is a flat 6-second cooldown at every rank, so it is never a window.
audit.why: Kit file: Rumble W cd '6'. Rumble's only true downtime is the Heat bar — at 100% Heat he Overheats and cannot cast spells at all.
audit.corrected: Gate the all-in on Overheat, not on Scrap Shield. Sylas 52.1% over 334 games; lane is tricky but not losing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a Sylas spike ('Hijack online — the all-in math and every 2v2 swing your way') while the packet chart and the content why both say Rumble controls 6.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30; The Equalizer is 130/105/80. At rank 1 his R outlasts yours by 50s, but he gets it first in the lane and it walls your only approach angle.
audit.corrected: Level 6 belongs to Rumble until you have hijacked The Equalizer. First item is a coin-flip on the hook. Two items is yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] describes 'Scrap Shield (W) move-speed removal'. Scrap Shield grants Rumble movement speed; it does not slow you. The slow is Electro-Harpoon.
audit.why: Riot text: W 'granting him a quick burst of speed'; E 'slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist'.
audit.corrected: Electro-Harpoon is 850 range against Chain Lash's 775 and Abscond/Kingslayer at 400 — he outranges every tool you own, and it shreds MR before Flamespitter lands.

audit.whatIsWrong: Multiple fields describe Sylas's E as providing a 'stun'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Abscond/Abduct is a dash with a recast pull; derived flags give projectile and dash only, no hardCC.
audit.corrected: Removed the stun claim from tradeBad; replaced it with the real loss condition (no shield, no gap-close, standing in the Flamespitter cone).

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown arithmetic anywhere despite it deciding the matchup.
audit.why: Flamespitter 10/9/8/7/6, Electro-Harpoon 0.5s per charge (2 charges), Scrap Shield 6s, The Equalizer 130/105/80 vs Hijack 80/55/30.
audit.corrected: Added the 80s/130s ultimate gap and the 6s Scrap Shield to breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull/dontsFull descriptions are copy-pasted off their own titles — dontsFull[2] is titled 'Sit on a stolen ult' but its body describes engaging with no E charges.
audit.why: Structural copy-paste from the generator; the page renders a title and an unrelated body.
audit.corrected: Rewrote dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d to match their titles with real numbers.

audit.why: suspectNames flags 'Run Flamespitter', 'Drop Equalizer', 'His Flamespitter', 'His Equalizer' — all four are correct usages of Flamespitter and The Equalizer, flagged on edit distance alone. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion.
audit.corrected: No name changes. All four are false positives.

edits.before: Hijack online — you now own a copy of Rumble's ultimate. The all-in math and every 2v2 swing your way.
edits.after: The Equalizer walls your approach — until you hijack it, his 130s R outlasts your 80s and he holds level 6.

edits.before: Riftmaker spike — your full chain with the W heal wins almost any extended 1v1 that starts even.
edits.after: Riftmaker is a coin-flip on the hook — land E2 and the W heal wins the brawl, miss it and he kites you.

edits.before: His Equalizer (R) blocks your engagement path the instant he hits 6; you need his R down or already stolen before you can safely all-in — he controls level 6.
edits.after: The Equalizer (R) walls off your approach the instant he hits 6, and at 130s it outlasts your 80s Hijack — until you have stolen it, he owns the level 6 window.

edits.before: Get on him with E2 the moment Scrap Shield is down — one full chain with the W heal erases a poke deficit.
edits.after: Go in when he Overheats — Scrap Shield is a 6s cooldown, so the real gate is his spell lock, then chain E2 into W.

edits.before: Erase his poke with W and kill him in one chained rotation. Shorthand: Scrap Shield down, wave right, go.
edits.after: Erase his poke with Kingslayer and kill him in one rotation. Shorthand: he Overheats, wave right, E2 and go.

edits.before: E2-engage only on Scrap Shield's cooldown
edits.after: E2-engage the moment his Heat locks him out

edits.before: Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Scrap Shield is back every 6s — no window. At 100% Heat he cannot cast, and that lock is your green light.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E1 shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rumble Heat: matchup-defining — Scrap Shield is a 6s cooldown, so his only downtime is Overheat, when he cannot cast for seconds. - Guard your E1 shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Hijack is 80s at rank 1 against his 130s Equalizer.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no gap-close, and you are a melee mage in Flamespitter's cone.

edits.before: Both E charges spent means no shield and no exit — you're a melee mage in the open.
edits.after: His Electro-Harpoon reaches 850 to your Chain Lash's 775 — you lose that exchange.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Hijack is 80s at rank 1 and his Equalizer is 130s — a stolen R you never cast is 80 seconds of nothing.

edits.before: Slow you with Scrap Shield (W) move-speed removal or Electro-Harpoon (E) so he can kite your E hook
edits.after: Kite with Scrap Shield (W) speed and Electro-Harpoon (E) slows at 850 range, outside every tool you own

notes: Level chart: full and content agreed with each other but both disagreed with the packet chart on rows 4, 5 and 6. Packet matches the whys text (whys[4] says he controls 6, whys[6] says Sylas owns late while win[6] said Rumble), so I moved both layers to the packet chart as one atomic six-edit group. All four suspectNames entries are false positives — Flamespitter and The Equalizer are the real names. The 'stun' language on Sylas's E is not supported by Riot's text; I removed it where I edited but it survives in breakdown.trading and report[3].t, which repeat the same tradeBad sentence.
